solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Business star about to manage light work

parts.note: CO, short for company

indicators.note: the star's name goes about, or around, the word for managing

parts.note: Mira is a variable star in the constellation Cetus
to cope is to manage or get by

explanation.surface: A celebrity entrepreneur turns to running things.
explanation.walkthrough: Mira is a named star, a favourite of setters; the light work is a genre of stage piece, not easy labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic opera is a light, humorous stage work set to music, as opposed to grand opera.

clue.text: Take off collar, back from party

parts.note: to collar a suspect is to arrest them, as is to cop them

indicators.note: the back of the word party is its final letter

parts.note: only its last letter is kept

explanation.surface: Someone removes their shirt collar after leaving a party.
explanation.walkthrough: To take off a person is to mimic them; collar is a verb meaning arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to imitate or mimic them, which is what a copycat does.

clue.text: Return of hit song Fever

indicators.note: the word for hit is turned to run back the other way

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit hard
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A hit single called Fever makes a comeback in the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Fever looks like the song's title, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria is a disease marked by recurring bouts of fever, once called ague.

clue.text: Commander on land inspiring serious fear

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the commander comes before the rest

parts.note: CO, the commanding officer

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the land takes the serious word inside it

parts.note: a nation is a country or land
stern means grave or serious

explanation.surface: A commanding officer coming ashore strikes terror into everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Consternation is alarm or dismay, a state of sudden anxious fear.

clue.text: Covering queen, bring up aristocratic adornment

indicators.note: the word for vomiting wraps around, or covers, the queen

parts.note: to puke is to vomit, to bring up food
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A courtier throws up over the queen while covering her.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A peruke is a powdered wig of the kind worn by gentlemen and nobility in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Low quality red tucked into by mistake

indicators.note: the red gem is eaten into, with the mistake placed inside it

parts.note: ruby is a deep red colour
bish is British slang for a blunder

explanation.surface: Something shoddy and red got eaten by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: Bish is informal British slang for a mistake, little known outside the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rubbishy is worthless or trashy, of poor standard.

clue.text: How feast begins with cut turkey

indicators.note: how something begins asks for its very start, here the opening of feast
the beginning of the word feast is its first letter

parts.note: the word supplies its opening letter only
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A holiday meal starts with carving the turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: Turkey here is the failed show or film, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A turkey is slang for a theatrical or commercial failure, which is a flop.

clue.text: Choose to delay opening service? Stand in church

indicators.note: the opening letter is held back until the end of the word

parts.note: to elect is to choose
the Royal Navy is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone opts to hold back the start of a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Service means a branch of the armed forces, not worship, despite the church setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is the reading desk in a church from which the lessons are read.

clue.text: Dick, Tommy and yours truly, we're told

parts.note: Tommy Atkins is the nickname for a British private soldier

indicators.note: said out loud, the setter's I is heard as the organ of sight

parts.note: the setter, so I

explanation.surface: A list of names, Dick and Tommy, plus the setter himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick is old slang for a detective; a Tommy is a British private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A private eye is a private detective, also called a dick in hard-boiled slang.

clue.text: Concerned with new blunder, knocked over drink

indicators.note: the whole string is toppled so it reads backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a slip is a small error

explanation.surface: A clumsy mistake causes someone to knock over their drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilsner is a pale lager beer, originally from Plzeň in Bohemia.

clue.text: Inch falteringly behind relative in narrow passages

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come after the relative

parts.note: bro, short for brother

indicators.note: moving falteringly, the letters stumble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone edges haltingly behind a family member through tight corridors.
explanation.definitionFit: The bronchi are the two main airways branching from the windpipe into the lungs.

clue.text: Crook, awful fiend in public, with excessive conviction

indicators.note: the crook and the rearranged fiend sit inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
a con is a convict or swindler

indicators.note: an awful mess of the word fiend, its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful villain shows himself openly, too sure of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Conviction is the definition's sense of certainty, even though crook suggests a court verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overconfident is to be too sure, having more certainty than is warranted.

clue.text: Common clothing turned to kind of blue or red

indicators.note: the common word dresses, or wraps around, the rest

parts.note: trite means commonplace, hackneyed

indicators.note: the little word is turned round

parts.note: taken as written
sky blue is a shade of blue

explanation.surface: Ordinary clothes are dyed blue or red.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trotskyite is a follower of Leon Trotsky, so a communist, a red.

clue.text: Character in Antigone say guzzled rolls

indicators.note: the word rolls over and is read backwards

parts.note: ate greedily

explanation.surface: An actor in Sophocles' tragedy wolfs down bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: Character means a letter of the Greek alphabet, the one Antigone is written in, not a person in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet, found in Greek text such as Antigone.

clue.text: Counterpart I see in uniform by medical department

indicators.note: the department sits next to the rest
the two letters go inside the word for uniform

parts.note: uniform as an adjective means unvarying, equal
taken as written
V, for vide, Latin for see
ENT, ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: Someone notices a matching outfit next to a hospital unit.
explanation.walkthrough: V stands for vide, used in references to mean see.
explanation.definitionFit: An equivalent is something corresponding in value or function, a counterpart.

clue.text: One's chased fancy car through waterfront area

indicators.note: the car runs through the middle of the waterfront

parts.note: a quay is a landing place by the water
RR, a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A police chase sees a luxury car speed along the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarry is the hunted animal or person, the prey being pursued.

clue.text: No chance to compose a stately dance tune

indicators.note: composing arranges these letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer has no hope of writing a dignified dance piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaconne is a slow, stately Baroque dance in triple time, and music written for it.

clue.text: Trip facilitator has setter endlessly climbing

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: scaling, as of a wall

explanation.surface: The setter keeps on climbing, enabling a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Trip means a drug-induced hallucination, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Mescalin is a hallucinogenic drug from the peyote cactus, which induces a psychedelic experience.

clue.text: Wearing suit, to a large extent

parts.note: dressed in something
spades is one of the four suits in cards

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in a business suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Suit here is a card suit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom in spades means in abundance or to a great degree.

clue.text: Hawking, say, with bird following animals around

indicators.note: the bird comes after the other part
the animals are turned around to read backwards

parts.note: pets are domestic animals
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Someone selling a bird, with animals around them.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawking looks like selling wares, but it is the physicist Stephen Hawking.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen is a first name, of which the physicist Stephen Hawking is an example.

clue.text: Superior copper wants start on case of sedition

indicators.note: the case letters are placed onto the shortened policeman
the outside letters of the word, like a case

parts.note: only its first and last letters are kept

indicators.note: the word lacks, or wants, its first letter

parts.note: a bobby is a British police officer

explanation.surface: A haughty policeman needs a way into a sedition case.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A snobby person acts superior, looking down on those of lower status.

clue.text: Spicy food this person thrice added to bran

indicators.note: the letters are added in among those of bran
thrice means the same letter for this person turns up three times over

parts.note: this person, from the setter's point of view, is I

explanation.surface: Someone adding spice three times to their bran breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Three I's are slotted among the letters of BRAN: after B, after R and at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiced Indian rice dish, more often spelt biryani, cooked with meat or vegetables.

clue.text: Silky material in African country changing hands

indicators.note: the left hand, L, is swapped for the right, R

parts.note: Angola in southwest Africa

explanation.surface: Fine cloth is traded in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R stand for left and right, the two hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is soft fibre from the angora rabbit or goat, used for silky yarn.

clue.text: A hundred euros initially, which is non-returnable

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the starting letter of euros is used

parts.note: only its first letter is kept

explanation.surface: A hundred euros paid up front cannot be refunded.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-returnable sounds like a refund policy; it is a tennis serve the opponent cannot hit back.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis an ace is a serve so good the receiver cannot return it.

clue.text: Uncovered van Gogh memoir — it's explosive

indicators.note: with its cover, the first and last letters, stripped off

parts.note: Vincent van Gogh, the painter
a diary is a personal record

explanation.surface: A newly discovered van Gogh memoir is causing a sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: An incendiary is a bomb or device designed to start fires, so something that ignites.

clue.text: Chinese dynasty's seventh child

parts.note: a son is a male child
G is the seventh letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An emperor's seventh child stood to inherit.
explanation.walkthrough: Seventh stands for G, the seventh letter of the alphabet; it is placed after the child in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Song was an imperial ruling house of China from 960 to 1279.

clue.text: What boozer craves more than old bottles

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer inside it, as a bottle holds a drink

parts.note: the run of letters across these words, from the end of more to the start of old

explanation.surface: A drunk wants a drink more than old bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottles looks like a noun for empties; it is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanol is the alcohol in beer, wine and spirits, the substance a drinker wants.

clue.text: Bagel flipping ass leaves in the kitchen

parts.note: a bagel is ring-shaped, like the letter O

indicators.note: the ass's name is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: an onager is a wild ass of Asia

explanation.surface: A donkey upsets a bagel and walks out of the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves seems a verb, someone departing; it is the noun, herb leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a herb whose dried leaves are used in cooking.

clue.text: One that bites back showing pronounced taste

indicators.note: the insect is turned back to front

parts.note: a gnat is a biting insect

explanation.surface: An animal that snaps back has a strong flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tang is a strong, sharp flavour or smell.

clue.text: An electrician's work is almost a disaster

definitions.meaning: ..., connecting a circuit to the ground for safety

explanation.walkthrough: The same letters split two ways: an earthing, and a near thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a close shave, while earthing is the grounding wiring job done by an electrician.
